headlines: Nebius Group (NBIS) Shares Plunge Nearly 14% Amid Tech Sector Selloff on November 20, 2026 — GuruFocus
Why Nebius Stock Is Falling Today Despite Strong AI Cloud Demand — Benzinga
Nebius Group (NBIS) Stock Price Prediction: Revenue cut, heavy selling, and a test of support — Blockchain.News
gappers.catalyst_detail: No NBIS-specific catalyst today. The move is the high-beta leg of a market-wide relief rally: Nasdaq-100 futures +3.0-3.4%, S&P futures +2.7%, breaking a seven-day S&P losing streak, with NVDA up roughly 10% premarket, China cutting margin requirements on borrowed-share purchases over the weekend and South Korea preparing a stabilisation fund. The stock-specific news is all older and all negative: on Nov 12 Nebius trimmed its 2026 revenue forecast on delays in third-party capacity additions, raised its capex plan and said it would lean on customer prepayments and asset-backed financing rather than fresh equity (shares -16%); Baird then cut its target to $200 from $340 while keeping Outperform, and Zacks downgraded to Hold on Nov 19. Friday's -16.1% to $81.31 was sector selling, not a new disclosure.
gappers.why: Mechanical beta snapback, not re-rating. NBIS is the most levered liquid proxy for the neocloud funding question, so when AI risk is sold it falls 2-4x the index and when the index bounces it retraces the same multiple. At +10.1% against QQQ's +3.7% premarket gap it is running ~2.7x the index — the same amplification factor in reverse. Short covering and the unwind of unusually expensive index put protection add a non-fundamental bid.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-to-three-day oversold bounce, not a sustainable turn. Premarket volume of 1.34M shares is real participation against a 31.2M 20-day average, so the bounce is not a thin-tape artifact — but it is also only ~4% of a normal day, which is not enough to call a reversal. The stock is 50.6% below its 50-SMA ($181.30) and 50.2% below its 200-SMA ($179.75); a +10% day does not approach either, so the long-bias filter still fails. The fundamental overhang that drove the de-rate (capacity delays, capex, funding mix) is unresolved. Read-through is to the whole neocloud complex, which is moving as one block — CRWV +7.9% is on this same list at rank 10.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Headline-free beta bounce off a 20.7%-ATR capitulation low, with the Nov 12 guidance cut still the operative fundamental fact; expect it to fade or chop rather than trend, and do not carry it past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — the account is 100% cash with 0 open positions, so the cost is one of three weekly trade slots and one of six position slots. Against today's own list it is the highest-gap name but the worst-quality setup: RKLB (rank 5) has a structural thesis and a 10.9% ATR versus NBIS's 20.7%. The decisive point is that it cannot clear the 2:1 minimum at a rule-legal stop: the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at $80.58, which is 0.53 ATR below entry — inside half a session's normal range, so noise takes it out before any thesis plays. A sane 1-ATR stop is $72.69 (-18.8%), which breaches the 10% rule outright, and the matching 2:1 target of $123.23 is still 58.9% below the 252-day high. No admissible version of this trade exists.

gappers.catalyst: ETH-proxy bounce after Friday's -13.87% close at $12.98; BitMine remains the #1 Ethereum treasury at 6.08M ETH (~99% of the way to 5% of supply) after adding 52,203 ETH last week.
headlines: Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) Announces ETH Holdings Reach 6.08 Million Tokens — OTC Markets
Bitmine Adds 52,203 ETH, Inches Closer to 5% of Ether Supply — CoinMarketCap
Why Is Bitmine Immersion Stock Falling on Friday? — Benzinga
gappers.catalyst_detail: No new company disclosure this morning. BitMine is a virtual-asset treasury company whose equity trades as a levered claim on its ETH stack: it holds 6.08M ETH, the largest Ethereum treasury, roughly 99% of the way to owning 5% of supply, having added 52,203 ETH last week at around $1,733/ETH. Friday it closed $12.98, -13.87%, which Benzinga attributed to crypto-linked equities declining broadly as ETH itself fell 6.49%; it then printed $13.40 (+3.24%) after hours. Today's +9.9% is the continuation of that after-hours bid alongside the general risk-on gap.
gappers.why: This is an ETH beta trade wearing an equity ticker. The mechanism is the treasury's mark: a move in ETH flows through to net asset value at roughly 1x and to the share price at more than 1x, because the market applies a swinging premium/discount to the stack on top. Friday's -13.9% on a -6.5% ETH day is that leverage; today's +9.9% is the same leverage unwinding. No operating result, contract or guidance is involved.
gappers.impact: Likely to mean-revert with ETH rather than hold on its own. Premarket volume of 899k against a 31.5M 20-day average is adequate but thin relative to the move. The stock closed Friday at $12.98 against a 252-day low of $12.80 — it bounced off the bottom of its entire year's range, which makes this a technical bounce with no fundamental floor beneath it except the ETH price. It sits 29.6% below its 200-SMA ($20.28) and 36.4% below its 50-SMA ($22.45), 66.1% off its 252-day high. The read-through is to every crypto treasury vehicle and to BLSH (+7.5% premarket, excluded from this list on thin premarket volume), so there is no idiosyncratic edge to capture here that an ETH position would not give more cheaply.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The entire thesis is the direction of ETH over the next few days; nothing structural changed at the company, and crypto-treasury vehicles map to no sector in the TRADING-STRATEGY.md rotation table, so there is no rotation phase to align with.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 open positions, 100% cash), so the cost is a weekly slot plus the correlation budget: a BMNR long is a concentrated crypto-beta bet that would block or crowd any later crypto-adjacent entry under the >0.75 correlation gate. Within today's list it ranks below RDW and RKLB on thesis quality despite a higher gap. R:R is borderline-admissible but unattractive: the 10% stop at $12.84 is 0.97 ATR, the tightest ratio on the top five, but that stop sits one cent above the 252-day low of $12.80, so it is a stop placed exactly where the whole market's sell orders already are. The 2:1 target off a 1-ATR stop is $17.23, 59.1% below the 252-day high — reachable in principle, but only on an ETH rally the setup gives no information about.

gappers.catalyst_detail: Redwire is the one name in today's top five with a genuine stock-specific fact set, though the immediate gap is still mostly beta. Q3 (Nov 4) missed on revenue at about $109M with a narrower-than-expected per-share loss; full-year revenue guidance was maintained and backlog hit a record $619.7M, up nearly 75% year over year — and the stock still fell roughly 19% the next day. Piper Sandler cut its target to $8 from $11 (neutral) on Nov 6. Since then: a roughly $40M award to supply the power generation system for NASA's planned moon base, a ~$15M contract for ELSA solar-array wings to AscendArc announced Nov 19, a follow-on U.S. Army order, and CEO Peter Cannito Jr. buying 14,144 shares on the open market at an average $7.07 on Nov 16. Cutting the other way, Wall Street Zen downgraded hold to sell this morning, Nov 23.
gappers.why: Two mechanisms are stacked. The dominant one is the same market-wide risk-on gap lifting every high-beta small cap. Underneath it is a real re-rating argument: a record backlog up 75% y/y plus three fresh awards plus a CEO buying stock with his own money at $7.07 is the 'insider signal' leg of the strategy's confluence rule, and it arrives while the stock trades at $6.16 — below the price the CEO paid eight days ago. The Wall Street Zen downgrade pushes against it but is a quant-model rating change, not new information about the business.
gappers.impact: The most plausible sustainable move on the list, and still not a clean one. Premarket volume of 217k against a 13.2M 20-day average is light — this is a beta lift on thin participation, not accumulation. Backlog and contract wins are durable facts that do not reverse when the tape turns, which separates RDW from NBIS and BMNR; but the stock is 42.8% below its 200-SMA ($10.77), 32.6% below its 50-SMA ($9.14), 76.9% off its 252-day high, and its Friday close of $5.65 is only 16% above a 252-day low of $4.87. RSI(14) at 30.2 is right at the oversold line. Sector read-through is to the small-cap space-infrastructure group, which is moving as a block today — RKLB, ASTS and LUNR all sit on this same list.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Unlike the rest of the top five, the catalyst set is structural rather than a headline — record backlog, three signed awards and an insider purchase are facts that persist after the bounce fades — and space/defense infrastructure maps to Industrials, a favored sector in the early-cycle row of the TRADING-STRATEGY.md rotation table; it would be worth a multi-day swing hold if it later clears the Confluence rule, which today it does not.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace — 100% cash, 0 positions — so the real cost is that RDW would consume one of three weekly trade slots and, being in the same space-infrastructure block as RKLB, ASTS and LUNR, would likely trip the >0.75 correlation gate against any second space name taken this week. That makes it a direct either/or with RKLB (rank 5), which has the larger franchise and a lower 12.4%-versus-10.9% ATR. On R:R, the 10% stop at $5.54 is 0.88 ATR — under one session's normal range, so it fails the practical test even though it is the second-best ratio here; a 1-ATR stop is $5.46 (-11.4%), already outside the 10% rule, and its 2:1 target of $7.56 is 71.6% below the 252-day high but above both the CEO's $7.07 basis and Piper's $8 target, so the target is at least credible. Not admissible today on the 200-SMA filter alone.

gappers.catalyst_detail: ASTS has the clearest single-name catalyst in today's top five: a Berenberg analyst initiated coverage with a $92 price target, a call published in the last several hours, framed as bullish despite the company's regulatory hurdles and heavy cash burn. A separate initiation the same week handed ASTS a $100 target while initiating Rocket Lab at neutral with $83. The stock closed Friday at $23.27, -8.92%, then printed $24.10 (+3.57%) after hours, and is quoted $25.37 premarket. There is no operational news — no launch, no contract, no regulatory decision — behind the move.
gappers.why: Sell-side sponsorship into an oversold tape. The mechanism is sentiment and positioning, not cash flow: a $92 target against a $25 price is a 263% implied upside headline, which draws momentum buyers and gives shorts a reason to cover in a name 81% off its 252-day high. The market-wide +3.7% QQQ gap supplies the rest. Note that the price-target gap itself is evidence of how little the initiation settles — no analyst model moves a stock from $25 to $92, and the cited risks (regulatory approvals, cash burn) are exactly the unresolved items.
gappers.impact: Most likely a one-to-two-day headline spike that fades. Premarket volume of 455k against an 18.8M 20-day average is unremarkable for a move this size. An initiation is a durable opinion but not a durable fact: it adds no revenue, no license and no funding, so there is nothing for the price to hold onto once the momentum flow is done — and ASTS already round-tripped a similar 12% pop earlier in the week per the same coverage. The technical position is the weakest on the list: 64.6% below its 200-SMA ($71.63), 45.0% below its 50-SMA ($46.10), RSI(14) 27.6, and Friday's close of $23.27 sits 2.4% above a 252-day low of $22.72. Read-through is to the satellite/space group — RKLB, RDW and LUNR are all on this list, and the same analyst note explicitly ranked ASTS above RKLB, which is part of why both are moving.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: An analyst initiation is a headline, not a structural change — nothing about the constellation, the regulatory path or the cash position moved — so expect the pop to fade within days and do not carry it past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions). The cost is a weekly slot spent on the lowest-quality thesis in the space block: taking ASTS would almost certainly block RDW or RKLB later in the week under the >0.75 correlation gate, and both have real contract-level facts where ASTS has an opinion. R:R is the second-worst on the list: the 10% stop at $22.83 is just 0.67 ATR — two-thirds of one session's normal range, and it sits essentially on the 252-day low, so it is both too tight and badly placed. A 1-ATR stop is $21.60 (-14.9%), outside the 10% rule, and the matching 2:1 target of $32.92 is 75.4% below the 252-day high. Not admissible.

gappers.catalyst: Bouncing after a seventh straight down day (-11% Friday to $45.42) triggered by a neutral-rating initiation at an $83 target; the CFO has guided to a 'very strong uplift' in Electron pricing within nine months off a record 54 launches booked in Q3.
headlines: CFO Sees 'Very Strong Uplift' In Electron Prices Within 9 Months, SpaceX Rideshare Slots Tighten — Stocktwits (Nov 23)
Cramer believes Rocket Lab's recent share-price weakness has created an opportunity — TheStreet
Prediction: Rocket Lab Will Triple Its Revenue by 2028 — The Globe and Mail
gappers.catalyst_detail: Rocket Lab fell nearly 11% on Friday to $45.42, its seventh consecutive daily decline, after a sell-side firm opened coverage at neutral with an $83 price target — the same note handed AST SpaceMobile a $100 target, so the move was a relative-preference call inside the space group rather than a judgement on the business. Pushing the other way, the CFO said over the weekend that Electron pricing should see a 'very strong uplift' within nine months, that the company booked a record 54 launches in Q3, and that SpaceX rideshare slots are tightening — which is the supply-side argument for that pricing power. Neutron remains the central growth catalyst; consensus is a strong buy with a 12-month target around $93, and Q4 results are due Mar 4. Cramer publicly framed the weakness as an opportunity.
gappers.why: A sentiment-driven seven-day unwind meeting a risk-on gap. The mechanism of Friday's drop was an analyst preference shift, not a business event; the mechanism of today's bounce is the market-wide relief rally plus the CFO's pricing commentary giving holders a reason to stop selling. Underneath both sits a genuine pricing-power story: if rideshare capacity on the only cheaper alternative is tightening while RKLB's launch book is at a record, per-launch price is the margin lever, and that is an operating fact rather than a target-price opinion.
gappers.impact: The most sustainable-looking move on today's list on both volume and structure. Premarket volume of 460k against a 19.0M 20-day average is ordinary, so the gap itself is beta rather than accumulation — but RKLB carries the lowest ATR on the top five at 10.9% of price and is the closest to its own trend, 19.4% below its 50-SMA ($61.34) against 23-51% for everything else here. It is still 36.4% below its 200-SMA ($77.72) and 67.2% off a $151 prior peak, with RSI(14) at 35.6 — oversold but not washed out, and Friday's close is 21% above the $37.57 52-week low rather than sitting on it like ASTS and BMNR. Read-through is to the launch/space complex, where ASTS, RDW and LUNR are all bouncing today; the fact that the whole group is moving together is the strongest evidence that today's gap is the tide, not the thesis.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Neutron, a record 54-launch Q3 book and a CFO-guided Electron price uplift are structural, and launch/space infrastructure sits in Industrials — a favored sector in the early-cycle row of the TRADING-STRATEGY.md rotation table — so this is the one name here worth a multi-day/week swing hold if it later clears the Confluence rule on a /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (100% cash, 0 positions), so the cost is one of three weekly trade slots and — because RKLB, RDW, ASTS and LUNR are one correlated space block — effectively the whole space allocation for the week under the >0.75 correlation gate. Ranked on thesis quality it is the name to spend that slot on, above RDW on franchise size and above NBIS/BMNR/ASTS outright. It still cannot clear 2:1 at a legal stop: the mandated 10% trailing stop at $44.51 is 0.99 ATR, the best ratio on this list but still inside one session's range, and it would have been hit on each of the last several days. A 1-ATR stop is $44.49 (-10.1%), fractionally outside the rule, and its 2:1 target of $59.40 is 60.7% below the 252-day high and below the ~$93 consensus target — the only target on this list that is genuinely reachable. The blocking failure is the 200-SMA long-bias filter, not the arithmetic.
